title: Declare every worker preparation with its own budget

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-340#declare-every-worker-preparation-with-its-own-budget at 44f1f86738b9c5b698ea4744d1c91c949357c6fa

VERDICT: Caught. Backend and E2E caught it. Integrated has no check that uses this path.

Promise (key example 3): "The three runner groups accept both queued host layouts, while one cold run proves timing, private copies and the later-revision override." The expected behavior is that the run-wide start-origin-codex-queued origin carries the Codex installation (.agents/skills/...) and start-origin-claude-queued carries the Claude installation (.claude/skills/...), in every group.

Clock: start 10:40:54 +08 (epoch ms 1794969654000). End sampled by finish-report.mjs: 1794969980879.

Fault (I changed the suggested fault): the suggestion was a swapped layout argument in the startOriginArtifacts registration. That argument also names the origin directory (path.join(directory, layout)), so swapping it would only cause an ENOENT crash when the origin is copied. To swap just the installed layout, I put the fault where the layout is applied. In dashboard/tests/support/startOriginPreparation.ts, prepareStartOrigin, `withInstallation(repository, layout, source)` became `withInstallation(repository, repository === runWideRepositories.queued && layout === "codex" ? "claude" : layout, source)`. The result is that the Codex queued origin keeps its key and its codex/ directory but contains Claude's installation. All three global setups (backend, integrated and e2e) register through the shared startOriginArtifacts(), so the fault reaches all three groups. I made one edit and left fixtures and assertions unchanged.

Independent wrong-behavior witness: a scratch script, bundled with esbuild and outside every test, called startOriginArtifacts().prepare for both queued keys and listed each bare origin's main tree. Under the fault, start-origin-codex-queued/codex had top paths ".claude/skills .gitignore .planning/...", the same as Claude's, and had no .agents/skills.

Commands (scratch worktree, `caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES <PROOF_RECORD>=... npm run --silent <script> -- <specs> --workers=1`, strict reporter, load avg about 3 to 3.6):
- Backend (test:dashboard:backend): runtime/test-preparation-budget.spec.ts and launches/agent-launch-preparation-codex-retry.spec.ts
- Integrated (test:dashboard:integrated): navigation/story-destination-repeat-cue.spec.ts
- E2E (test:e2e): intent/intent-ci-comparison-retry.spec.ts and launches/agent-launch-preparation-codex.spec.ts (I added this as the nearest E2E consumer of the Codex queued origin's content)

Baseline (passed and exercised, per the proof records): Backend 11/11, Integrated 1/1, E2E 3/3.

Faulted run:
- Backend: failed, 11/11. The catch for the shared preparation is test-preparation-budget.spec.ts:128, `expect(onClaude?.tree).not.toEqual(onCodex?.tree)`, in the one cold nested run under backendGlobalSetup.ts. The Codex case's private copy had [".claude", ".gitignore", ".planning", "trunk.txt"], identical to the Claude tree. All 10 Codex retry cases also failed at agent-launch-preparation-codex-retry.spec.ts:54, `expect(profiles).toHaveLength(1)` (received []).
- E2E: failed, 1 of 3. agent-launch-preparation-codex.spec.ts:55, `expect(dialog).toContainText("Start also publishes")`, failed because the Codex dialog reported that the installed skills do not start refinement with a session policy for this host and that dough-story-refinement has no options file. Both intent-ci-comparison-retry cases passed: they only request the Codex queued key through queuedOriginsReady and run on the Claude host.
- Integrated: passed, 1/1. The repeat-cue journey only awaits queuedOriginsReady and uses the Claude host. No Integrated spec sets preparationHost "codex" (grep found it only in support/preparationPage.ts and the Backend nested fixture). In Integrated the faulted Codex origin is prepared but never consumed, so this is not an assertion gap: no Integrated check takes the faulted path.

Bounds: the catch is limited to the observed paths, which are the shared preparation code (Backend budget spec) and E2E's Codex launch. At this revision all three setups spread the same startOriginArtifacts(), so a per-group layout swap in one global-setup Map is not structurally possible. I did not repeat execution's omitted-key fault.

Restoration: I ran `git checkout --` on the file and cmp matched it byte for byte to the pre-probe copy. `git status --porcelain` was empty at HEAD 44f1f8673 before the probe and again after restoration. The rerun of the same commands passed: Backend 11/11, Integrated 1/1, E2E 3/3. I removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove` (it is no longer listed and the directory is gone) and deleted the witness files. I made no edits in the execution worktree.

Next proof action: none is needed for this promise. The current Backend cold run (line 128) and E2E's Codex launch journey already catch a Codex queued origin built with the Claude layout. If you want per-group content proof for Integrated, that is a separate decision, because Integrated has no Codex queued consumer today. No planned repair or earlier disposition applies.

Cost:
- Test runtime (measured, runner durationMs from proof records): baseline 43.4 s, faulted 33.5 s, restored 37.0 s; total about 114 s. npm ci is not included and was not measured.
- Human effort: unavailable. There was no human involvement to measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No token or time meter is available to this agent. About 35 tool calls, a count and not a time measure.
- Invocation-to-report elapsed (measured): 326879 ms (about 5.4 min), from 1794969654000 to 1794969980879 in Unix epoch ms.

Wrap-up disposition: 44f1f86738b9c5b698ea4744d1c91c949357c6fa, Caught, no follow-up.
